title: Exact four-term row of regular power quotient module sheaves
statement: Let $(C,J)$ be a site essentially small in the coefficient universe, let $R$ be a commutative ring sheaf and $t$ a global section injective by multiplication on each $R(U)$. Use the canonical power quotients and scalar maps of [def-sp-regular-scalar-quotient-notation]. For natural $m\leq n$ there are a ring reduction $r:B_n\to B_m$ with $p_n r=p_m$ and a $B_n$-linear map $a:r_*B_m\to B_n$ satisfying $a(p_m(x))=p_n(t^{n-m}x)$ on every section. The row $0\to r_*B_m\xrightarrow{a}B_n\xrightarrow{t^{m+1}}B_n\xrightarrow{r}r_*B_m\to0$ is exact. The image subobject of $a$ is the image of multiplication by $t^{n-m}$. When $n=m$, $r$ and $a$ are identities under the canonical equality transports and multiplication by $t^{m+1}$ on $B_n$ is zero. No complexes, augmentations or K-flatness are asserted.

proof.text: Put $Q_k(U)=R(U)/t^kR(U)$. For $A=R(U)$ and $d=n-m\geq0$, define $Q_m(U)\to Q_n(U)$ by $[x]\mapsto[t^dx]$. Replacing $x$ by $x+t^my$ changes its image by $t^{d+m}y=t^ny$, so it is well-defined. It is $A/t^nA$-linear because $[t^d(rx)]=[r]\,[t^dx]$, with $A/t^nA$ acting on $A/t^mA$ by reduction. If $t^dx=t^ny$, cancel $t^d$ to obtain $x=t^my$; cancellation for $d=0$ is the identity. Thus this map is injective. All formulas commute with restrictions, since $t$ is global.

proof.text: In the same ring $A$, if $t^m[x]=0$ in $A/t^nA$, write $t^mx=t^ny=t^m t^{n-m}y$ and cancel $t^m$: then $x=t^{n-m}y$. Conversely every such $x$ is killed by $t^m$. Hence the first image is precisely the kernel of the middle map and is $t^{n-m}(A/t^nA)$. Also $[x]$ reduces to zero in $A/t^mA$ exactly when $x=t^my$ for some $y\in A$, which is precisely the image of the middle map. Reduction is surjective, by lifting $[x]$ to $[x]$ modulo $t^n$. Together with step 4 this proves the whole presheaf row is sectionwise exact.

proof.text: Sheafify the presheaf row of steps 4–5 as presheaves of $R$-modules using [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact]. The resulting terms are exactly $B_m,B_n,B_n,B_m$, and the universal property [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] gives the maps $a_{n,m}$, $t^m$ and reduction, uniquely with their stated local formulas. For the $B_n$-module structures, $Q_n$ is a presheaf of commutative rings whose ring sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] is the quotient ring sheaf $B_n$, and $Q_m,Q_n$ are presheaves of $Q_n$-modules, with the three maps $Q_n$-linear by step 4. Apply [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] with $\mathcal O=Q_n$: the abelian sheafifications $B_m,B_n$ of $Q_m,Q_n$ receive unique compatible $B_n$-module structures, and the three maps, being the unique factorizations of $Q_n$-linear presheaf maps, are $B_n$-linear. For $\mathcal P=Q_n$, the factorization $\mathcal P^\#\to B_n$ of the ring unit $Q_n\to B_n$ is $B_n$-linear and, on underlying sets, is the comparison of two sheafifications of $|Q_n|$ [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets]; so it is bijective and the module $B_n$ is the regular module. Kernels and sheafified cokernels in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], for the sheaf of rings $B_n$, are those of the underlying abelian sheaves, so the exact row is exact as $B_n$-modules. Its first image is $t^{n-m}B_n$: both are the sheafification of the presheaf image calculated in step 5. If $n=m$, the exponent $n-m$ is zero, so $a_{m,m}=1$, reduction is $1$, and $t^m=0$ on $B_m$; the row becomes $0\to B_m\xrightarrow{1}B_m\xrightarrow{0}B_m\xrightarrow{1}B_m\to0$.

theorem regularScalarQuotient_moduleRow
    (hregular : ∀ U : Cᵒᵖ, Function.Injective
      (fun x : R.obj.obj U ↦ (@id (R.obj.obj U) (t.val U)) * x)) (n m : ℕ) (hm : m ≤ n) :
    ∃ red : B R t n ⟶ B R t m,
      projection R t n ≫ red = projection R t m ∧
      ∃ (a : (res red).obj (unit (B R t m)) ⟶ unit (B R t n)),
        (∀ (U : Cᵒᵖ) (x : R.obj.obj U),
          a.val.app U ((projection R t m).hom.app U x) =
            (projection R t n).hom.app U ((@id (R.obj.obj U) (t.val U)) ^ (n - m) * x)) ∧
        Mono a ∧ Epi (ringMap red) ∧
        (∃ ha : a ≫ mul (B R t n) (scalarImage R t (projection R t n))
            (unit (B R t n)) (m + 1) = 0,
          (ShortComplex.mk a (mul (B R t n) (scalarImage R t (projection R t n))
            (unit (B R t n)) (m + 1)) ha).Exact) ∧
        (∃ hb : mul (B R t n) (scalarImage R t (projection R t n))
            (unit (B R t n)) (m + 1) ≫ ringMap red = 0,
          (ShortComplex.mk (mul (B R t n) (scalarImage R t (projection R t n))
            (unit (B R t n)) (m + 1)) (ringMap red) hb).Exact) ∧
        imageSubobject a = imageSubobject
          (mul (B R t n) (scalarImage R t (projection R t n))
            (unit (B R t n)) (n - m)) ∧
        (∀ h : n = m,
          red = eqToHom (congrArg (B R t) h) ∧
          (∀ (U : Cᵒᵖ) (x : (B R t m).obj.obj U),
            a.val.app U x = (eqToHom (congrArg (B R t) h.symm)).hom.app U x) ∧
          mul (B R t n) (scalarImage R t (projection R t n))
            (unit (B R t n)) (m + 1) = 0)
